run.market_summary: 1) A hawkish Fed turn is the main theme. Inflation has beaten forecasts for a third straight month, producer prices jumped 6.5%, the Fed's Collins is talking about "gradual" hikes, and a December hike is now in play. That is lifting the dollar and pushing bond prices down. Stocks are ignoring it so far (SPY +2.6%, QQQ +3.6% over 5 days). That gap is the risk, but trading against an index rally purely on the model's score is a weak bet. 2) Nvidia is in a governance and regulatory crisis: Huang has resigned, the Treasury has given the company 10 days to explain alleged China chip sales, and a spy scandal involves Lutnick. Money is moving out of NVDA (-12.7%) into AMD, AMAT and LRCX (+11–19%), so the 'export controls hurt all chips' idea is being contradicted by prices outside NVDA. 3) Geopolitics: Iran's drone strike on a US base in Bahrain is a real escalation, but oil still fell 1.9% over 5 days. Defense stocks have already rallied about 4–5%, and the Xi-Trump-Putin summit could ease tensions. China's October data missed across the board, but in China bad data tends to raise hopes of more stimulus rather than push stocks lower.

ideas.thesis: A third straight inflation beat plus a 6.5% producer-price jump, and Collins openly talking about 'gradual' hikes, mean the market still has to price in a hiking cycle into the December FOMC. This is the cleanest way to express the strongest macro signal (monetary_policy +0.47, inflation +0.29).

Fed hike bets are lifting the dollar against currencies whose central banks are still on hold ('Yen Slumps as Fed Rate-Hike Bets Boost Dollar'), and a Middle East escalation adds some safe-haven demand. Compared with TLT, this bets on the Fed being tighter than other central banks rather than on duration, but the two are correlated, so size them together.

Huang has resigned, the Treasury has set a 10-day deadline over alleged China chip sales, and the Lutnick spy-scandal questions are still unresolved. This is a stock-specific overhang with a dated catalyst and an open-ended CEO search, which is cleaner than shorting the whole chip sector while the rest of it rallies.

If the Fed really does start hiking, small caps are the most exposed part of the stock market because they carry more floating-rate debt, and they have barely joined the rally (+1.4%). This is the one equity short we keep to express the 'stocks are ignoring rate hikes' gap.

analysis.headline: An AI-led sell-off sent the Nasdaq down 2.5% into correction territory: semis gapped lower on Nvidia's leadership crisis and a new US rule limiting China's access to AI chips, then selling spread across the market intraday ahead of Nvidia earnings and the Anthropic IPO, while crypto, copper and oil fell too.
analysis.narrative:
Few index moves were statistically extreme. SPY fell 1.9% (z -1.4) and QQQ 2.7% (z -1.2), but the selling was broad: 2 of 13 sector ETFs rose, decliners outnumbered advancers about 3.2 to 1, and the VIX rose about 19%. Reuters reported that the Nasdaq closed more than 10% below its October 6 record, which puts it in a correction. The damage before the open was concentrated in chips. SMH gapped down 3.7%, AMAT and LRCX about 5-6%, AVGO 4.1% and NVDA 2.4%. Asian chip stocks had sold off overnight, the administration issued a new rule restricting China's access to top AI chips (per Reuters/Korea Times), and the weekend's Huang/Lutnick scandal kept pushing Congress toward tighter curbs. During the session, CNBC reported that Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Huang back. Selling then spread to the rest of the AI complex: GOOGL fell 4.1%, AMZN 3.3%, META 2.4%, and CoreWeave, Dell, SMCI, Micron and Intel each fell 6% or more. Traders were reducing risk before Nvidia reports on Tuesday under interim CEO Kress and before Anthropic's roughly $1.4T IPO on Thursday. Alphabet and Amazon each own more than 5% of Anthropic.

Defensive sectors (XLP, XLV, XLU, XLRE) opened higher but gave back gains during the day. Banks gave up an opening gain after app outages at Chase, BofA and Wells were reported in the afternoon. The rate story did not drive today. The 10-year fell 3 bp to 5.12% and TLT finished flat, so this was not a hawkish-Fed sell-off even though a December hike is priced at roughly 94%. The dollar rose slightly and gold fell another 0.8%, which fits the hawkish backdrop continuing, not a new shock. Treasuries acted as a mild hedge.

The moves that were statistically unusual came from other risk assets. Bitcoin hit its weekend low near $62-64k. Crypto equities gapped lower at the open: IBIT -5.5% (z -2.3), MSTR -7.7% (MSCI index removal pending), COIN -6.1% and HOOD -7.5%. HOOD was hit a second time by a report that Kalshi is moving into stock trading. Copper fell to a four-month low as the AI sell-off combined with China's broad October data miss (Bloomberg). That took FCX down 6.8% (z -2.2), along with BABA, EEM and the miners. CAT fell 5% as part of the "AI-linked industrial" trade. WTI fell 3.6%, all of it during the session, as shipments through the Strait of Hormuz recovered. That outweighed the Iran-Bahrain strike and the third US carrier in the region. Energy stocks and defense (ITA -2.5%) fell along with it.

drivers.evidence: Yahoo Finance live blog: NVDA fell about 4% after a CNBC report that the board is not considering bringing Huang back. TradingKey 12:55 headline. Korea Times/Reuters: NVDA -4.2%, the worst of the Magnificent Seven.

drivers.driver: New US rule restricting China's access to advanced AI chips, plus congressional pressure for tighter curbs after the scandal
drivers.evidence: Reuters (via Korea Times): the administration issued a new rule restricting China's access to top AI chips before the Trump-Xi meeting. FT/Newsmax weekend reports on Congress tightening rules. The Information: Chinese AI stocks plunged. The SMH gap (-3.7%) and AMAT/LRCX gaps (-5% to -6%) point to overnight news hitting the whole sector.

drivers.driver: Risk reduction across AI stocks before the Nvidia print and the roughly $1.4T Anthropic IPO, which raises supply and AI-funding worries
drivers.evidence: Bloomberg: 'Nasdaq 100 Plunges as Nvidia Earnings, Anthropic IPO on Horizon'. Kiplinger: 'Nasdaq Falls 626 Points to Start Nvidia-Anthropic Week'. IMF's Georgieva warned about $1T of circular AI financing. CoreWeave, Nebius, Dell and SMCI fell 6-7%. GOOGL and AMZN, both Anthropic holders, fell 3-4% during the session.

drivers.evidence: Bloomberg 11/16: 'Copper Sinks to Four-Month Low on Tech Rout, China Growth Woes'. Reuters/CNBC: industrial output, retail sales and fixed-asset investment all missed. StockStory: FCX, Vale, BHP and Albemarle traded down.

drivers.driver: Oil fell as shipments through the Strait of Hormuz recovered, outweighing the Iran-Bahrain escalation
drivers.evidence: Yahoo Finance live blog: Brent fell to about $92 as Hormuz shipments recovered despite the larger US military presence. Laodong: a possible 3.8 mb/d surplus. All of WTI's -3.6% came during the session.

drivers.evidence: Investing.com: 'Robinhood, Schwab shares slip as Kalshi prepares to enter stock trading'. TradingView: HOOD 'slides further after report'.

analysis.cross_asset_read: This was risk-off driven by equities and AI, not by rates. The VIX rose about 19%, but the 10-year fell 3 bp and TLT was flat, so bonds acted as a mild hedge, not the source of the selling. That rules out the hawkish-Fed story as today's driver. The dollar rose 0.2% and gold fell 0.8%, extending the hawkish Fed trend, but neither move was unusual. Oil fell with defense stocks, which shows supply relief (Hormuz flows) outweighing the Iran headlines. Copper, FCX, EEM and BABA fell together, consistent with the China growth miss plus the AI-capex unwind. Crypto equities fell more than bitcoin itself (BTC was nearly flat on the day), so the ETFs and stocks were catching up to the weekend drop at the open. Defensive sectors opening higher shows rotation at the open, but they faded with everything else.

axis_realized.note: New rule restricting China's AI-chip access plus congressional momentum. Semis and chip equipment gapped 4-6% lower across the sector.
China's October data miss pushed copper to a four-month low. FCX, BABA and EEM fell. Bad data did not lift stocks on stimulus hopes.
Hormuz shipments recovering. WTI -3.6% during the session. XLE, XOM and OXY lower.
Hawkish backdrop (about 94% priced for December) showed in a stronger dollar and weaker gold, but yields fell, so it was not a driver today.
Iran-Bahrain escalation was ignored. Oil and defense fell, and Hormuz flows are normalizing.

model_grade.summary: The trade ideas mostly worked (NVDA short, IWM short and UUP long all paid; TLT short was flat), but the theme ranking was wrong. Monetary policy, the model's top theme, did not drive prices, since yields fell. The chip-equipment rotation thesis broke when export controls hit the whole sector. The model also called oil and geopolitics tighter, and it missed crypto, the Anthropic IPO supply and the copper/China read.
got_right: SHORT NVDA: the stock fell 4.1% on the leadership overhang, as the model's thesis expected
LONG UUP: +0.2%, a small gain, beating SPY by about 2.1%
chip_export_controls was the highest-scored theme, and the policy channel did hit prices
Warning that the index rally was fragile
got_wrong: The NVDA-to-AMAT/LRCX/AMD rotation thesis: AMAT -5.5% and LRCX -6.7% as export controls hit the whole sector
Ranking monetary_policy (+0.47) as the main theme: the 10-year fell 3 bp and TLT was flat, so the SHORT TLT idea went nowhere
energy_supply +0.20 and geopolitical_conflict +0.36: oil fell 3.6% and defense fell 2.5%
'Bad China data = stimulus hopes': copper, FCX, BABA and EEM all fell on it
missed: Bitcoin falling to $62-64k plus MSTR's MSCI removal: the most statistically unusual moves of the day (IBIT, MSTR, COIN, HOOD)
Selling ahead of the Anthropic IPO and Nvidia earnings across the AI complex (GOOGL, AMZN, CoreWeave, Dell)
Copper at a four-month low hitting miners and CAT
Hormuz flows recovering and pushing oil down
Kalshi entering stock trading (HOOD) and the bank app outages

lessons: When the export-control score is high, apply it to the whole semis/chip-equipment group, not just the named company. Five-day dispersion (equipment stocks up while NVDA fell) can reverse sharply when a policy rule hits the sector.
Lower the weight on monetary_policy for duration trades when an equity drawdown catalyst (earnings, IPO supply) is also scored. On risk-off days, Treasuries hedge and a SHORT TLT idea stalls.
Add a crypto-beta tracker (BTC weekend move, MSTR index events) so the model sees Monday gaps in IBIT, COIN, MSTR and HOOD before the open.
Score energy_supply from physical flow news (Hormuz shipments, surplus estimates) as well as conflict headlines. Escalation without supply disruption has repeatedly failed to lift oil.
Treat a weak China data print as negative for copper and FCX, not as a stimulus-hope positive, unless a policy announcement comes with it.
Flag scheduled supply and catalyst events (mega-IPO, bellwether earnings) as de-risking drivers for AI-linked stocks in the sessions before them.
